newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Afghan official says gov't retreating from Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghan official says gov't retreating from Kabul.

text.p: Aghanistan's deputy foreign minister said on Thursday that government troops were leaving Kabul and the president was considering transferring power on Friday.

Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai said that the country's military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, had gone north of the city, taking with him jet fighters and other military hardware. The president, Burhanuddin Rabbani, he said was on the outskirts of the capital and would decide on Friday about a "transfer of power."

Reports from Kabul have said that the country's rebel Taleban Islamic milita appeared poised to capture Kabul, having seized the main government airbase north of the capital and taking parts of the city.
"Masood has decided to retreat to territory north of the city because he didn't want Kabul city to turn into a blood bath," the minister told Reuters Television in an interview.

"The president is in the outskirts to the north and by tomorrow will announce his decision, whether to leave the capital," he said adding that the president would take the advice of other members of his high council.

He said he thought "there will be a transfer of power, to whom we do not know," adding that he would be consulting with members of his high council. He said he hoped that Afghan's former King, Zahir Shah, ousted in 1973 and now in Rome, would return to the country as even the Taliban would accept him in a leadership role.
